subject: Re: Order form indemnity — defend vs reimburse; propose insurance-bridge
messages:
From: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@greengridsystems.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: GreenGrid Legal <legal@greengridsystems.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form indemnity — defend vs reimburse; urgent ask

Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and legal have a couple of last outstanding items on the order form indemnity that are blocking signature: specifically GreenGrid needs: 1) clarity that Redwood will defend third-party IP infringement claims for delivered models/services (not just reimbursement), 2) an explicit insurance offset cap (we want Redwood's indemnity to be reduced by the amount paid by your insurer), and 3) an exceptions carveout for customer-provided data / customer modifications.

I've attached our procurement note (GG_Indemnity_Request_10192026.pdf) and a short DLP/Q&A spreadsheet (GreenGrid_DLP_QA.xlsx) that explains how our customers instrument the model in production. Two asks from us:
- Can Redwood accept defend-and-control for third-party IP claims limited to the model as delivered, with standard cooperation language?
- Can we accept an insurer-offset clause (so insurance proceeds reduce indemnity recoveries) and also keep the overall cap in line with our order form?

We are on a tight timeline (deal to legal by 10/23) — can you confirm whether this is feasible and who on your side will own the redline conversation? If it helps, we can jump on a short call.

Best,
Alyssa Tran
Head of Procurement, GreenGrid Systems
Alyssa.Tran@greengridsystems.com

Attachments: GG_Indemnity_Request_10192026.pdf, GreenGrid_DLP_QA.xlsx

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form indemnity — defend vs reimburse; propose insurance-bridge

Hi Alyssa —

Appreciate the clear ask and attachments. Quick response: Redwood's default position is to offer "defend and control" for third-party IP claims for the product as delivered, with the standard cooperation and mitigation obligations from the customer. We typically limit indemnity where the claim arises from customer modifications or from customer-provided data — happy to reflect that in the redline.

Regarding insurance offset: we usually accept a clause that allows insurance proceeds to be considered in the calculation of recoverable amounts, but we don't agree to a blanket dollar-for-dollar offset that would effectively obviate Redwood's duty to indemnify. That said, given your timeline and enterprise procurement posture, I'm prepared to surface a compromise to legal: an "insurance-bridge" approach (see below) that gives GreenGrid comfort now and lets us finalize a tailored cap/offset during contract execution.

Proposed short plan:
- I will loop in Legal (Kimberly) and Contracts (Rishi) to prepare a redline with: defend-and-control limited to delivered model; explicit carveouts for customer modifications; an insurance-offset provision that preserves Redwood's primary indemnity but allows recovery calculation to net insurer payments up to the policy limit; and a temporary bridge concession for procurement to sign-off.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow (10/21) with your legal team?

I'll attach the draft redline once legal and contracts have reviewed.

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Order form indemnity — defend vs reimburse; propose insurance-bridge

Sofia / Rishi —

Thanks for flagging. Quick legal take and suggested compromise language to include in the redline:

High-level position:
- Defend-and-control for third-party IP claims that relate to the model "as delivered" (i.e., not modified by Customer and not arising from Customer data) — we accept.
- Carveouts: Customer misuse, Customer modifications, and Customer-provided data remain outside Redwood's indemnity.
- Cap: maintain order-form cap, but allow calculation of indemnity recoveries to be net of insurance proceeds (i.e., insurer payments reduce Redwood's exposure).

Suggested redline snippet (draft):
"Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer against any third-party claim alleging that the Services, as delivered by Redwood and used in accordance with the Documentation, infringe a third party's intellectual property rights. Redwood's obligations do not extend to Claims arising from (a) Customer modifications to the Services, (b) Customer-provided data or training materials, or (c) Customer misuse. To the extent Redwood receives payment under any insurance policy in respect of such Claim, Redwood's indemnity obligations hereunder shall be reduced by the amount of such insurance proceeds paid to the Customer; provided that such reduction shall not relieve Redwood of its obligation to defend."

Question for Contracts: do we want to offer a temporary insurance-bridge where Redwood agrees to a higher interim cap for signature, which drops back to the order-form cap once insurance confirmation is provided? Rishi / Ops: is that operationally feasible?

I'll attach a tracked redline for the order form.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-22T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Order form indemnity — defend vs reimburse; propose insurance-bridge

Kim / Sofia —

Operationally we can support an "insurance-bridge" as a limited procurement concession: offer GreenGrid an interim increase to the cap for signature conditioned on (a) written confirmation of Redwood's cyber/IP insurance (policy declaration page) within 30 days post-signature, and (b) a covenant from customer to provide notice and cooperate with insurer claims. After 30 days, if insurance evidence is not provided, we revert to the standard order-form cap. The mechanics: we would accept netting of insurer proceeds against indemnity recoveries but retain the duty to defend.

I'll prepare the redline (GG_Indemnity_Redline_v1.docx) with:
- The defend-and-control paragraph Kim suggested,
- Bridge clause language with a 30-day insurance evidence window, and
- Carveouts for customer modifications and data.

If you both sign off I can send to Alyssa and propose the 10/23 cutover.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Contracts & Operations, Redwood Inference
